title: Concealment of income in maintenance cases - how courts catch it
p1:
Think someone can simply hide their income and avoid paying fair maintenance?

Many people assume courts only look at salary slips. That is one of the biggest misconceptions in maintenance cases.
p2:
Courts often look beyond the documents presented. A person may show a low official income, but their lifestyle, expenses, assets, business activities, bank records, and spending patterns can tell a different story.

A surprising fact: even social media posts showing expensive purchases, frequent travel, or a high standard of living can sometimes become relevant clues.
p3:
The idea is simple: maintenance decisions are based on the real financial capacity of a person, not just a single piece of paper. Courts can compare declared income with actual lifestyle and available evidence to identify inconsistencies.

The practical lesson? Hiding income may delay the process, but it can damage credibility when the truth comes out.
conclusion: Do you think courts should rely more on official income documents or lifestyle evidence when deciding maintenance amounts?
